heading: Who has John 18:31?
greek: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑμῶν κρίνατε αὐτόν. εἶπον αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· ἡμῖν οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἀποκτεῖναι οὐδένα·
translation: So Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law.” The Jews said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death.”

witnesses.contents: John 18:31–33 (front) and 18:37–38 (back). A scrap about the size of a credit card (8.9 × 6.4 cm) from a codex, not a scroll.

A nearly complete codex of John 1–14; chapters 15–21 survive only as damaged fragments. John 18:31 lies inside the surviving range, but which letters of it are legible should be checked against the facsimile.
Gospels, Acts, Catholic Epistles and Paul (to Hebrews 9:14). John is complete.
Complete New Testament, plus much of the Greek Old Testament. John 18:31 is on a fully preserved page.
The four Gospels in the ‘Western’ order Matthew, John, Luke, Mark. John 14:26–16:7 is missing; John 18 survives.
Greek Old and New Testament, with gaps. In John only 6:50–8:52 is missing.
Parts of every New Testament book. In John, 18:36–20:25 is lost, but 18:31 survives just before the gap.
Three leaves: Matthew 1:23–2:2, 19:3–8, 21:19–24 and John 18:29–35.
Fragments of John 16:29–19:26. Fragments 11–15 preserve John 18:23–27, 31, 34–35 and 37.
Two leaves: John 16:30–17:9 and 18:31–40. Our verse is the first line of the second leaf.
Scattered parts of all four Gospels. For John 18 the surviving text includes 18:1–9, 11–13, 18–24, 28–29, 31 and 36 onward.
The four Gospels with a few gaps in Luke. John is complete.
The four Gospels with some gaps. In John only 21:15–25 is missing.
The four Gospels with gaps. John breaks off at 18:34, so 18:31 is among the last surviving verses.
Six leaves with John 16:3–19:41 (published lists vary on the exact starting verse), accompanied by a commentary.
A complete text of the four Gospels.
The four Gospels with gaps. In John, 18:5–19 and 19:4–27 are missing; 18:31 survives between the two gaps.
The four Gospels with gaps. In John, 9:30–10:25, 18:2–18 and 20:12–25 are missing; 18:31 survives.
The four Gospels, complete.
The four Gospels, complete.
The four Gospels, complete.
The four Gospels with gaps. In John only 20:27–21:17 is missing.
The four Gospels; the gaps are all in Matthew.
Luke and John. Matthew and Mark from the same book are minuscule 566, now in St Petersburg.
The four Gospels with small gaps. In John, 6:15–35, 8:6–39 and 9:21–10:3 are missing, and 21:22–25 was added later; 18:31 is original.
The four Gospels, complete.
The four Gospels in Greek with a Latin translation written word-for-word above the lines. In John, 19:17–35 is missing; 18:31 survives.
Eight leaves with John 18:4–20:2.
Gospels from Mark 9:5 onward, Acts, Catholic Epistles and Paul. John is complete.

excluded.reason: The original Greek leaves for John 18:14–20:13 are lost. The gap was filled in later by another hand, so the text here is not the 5th-century copy.
The purple codex is scattered across several libraries; nothing survives between John 16:15 and 20:23.
A palimpsest; only John 1:29–40, 2:13–25 and 21:1–11 survive.
Greek text of John survives only as far as 8:31.
The majuscule hand stops at John 8:39; the rest was supplied in minuscule in the 13th century.
Starts at John 18:36, just after our verse.
All contain John 18 but fall after the AD 900 cut-off for this first version. (028 S is precisely dated to 949 by its scribe’s note.)
Hundreds of later copies contain the verse. They are planned for a later version as a searchable list.
